text: A certain woman, the wife of one of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. Now the creditor has come to take my two boys as his slaves."
Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She answered, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil."
Then he said, "Go out and borrow vessels from all your neighbors—empty vessels, and don't ask for just a few.

versions.text: Then he said, "Go, borrow vessels from everyone outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels, and don't be sparing.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מִן־הַחוּץ means "from outside" (i.e., out of the house), not "from everyone outside," which duplicates and confuses the following phrase "from all your neighbors." Also אַל־תַּמְעִיטִי is a warning not to gather too few, which "don't ask for just a few" conveys more clearly for oral reading.

text: Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these vessels, setting aside each one as it is filled."
So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons, and while they kept bringing the vessels to her, she kept pouring.

versions.text: So she left him, shut the door behind herself and her sons, and while they kept bringing the vessels to her, she kept pouring.
versions.explanation: "Behind herself" is awkward when read aloud; "behind her and her sons" is smoother and equally accurate.

text: When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." But he said to her, "There are no more." Then the oil stopped.
She came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; you and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha was passing through Shunem, where a wealthy woman lived, and she urged him to stay for a meal. So whenever he passed by, he would stop there to eat.
She said to her husband, "I know that this man who so often comes our way is a holy man of God.
Let's build a small room on the roof and put a bed there for him, with a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us he can stay there."
One day when he came, he went up to the room and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she stood before him.

Elisha said to him, "Tell her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Should a word be spoken on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."
"What then can be done for her?" he asked. Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
Then he said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
And Elisha said, "About this time next year you will hold a son in your arms." "No, my lord, man of God," she said, "do not deceive your servant."

versions.text: And Elisha said, "About this time next year you will hold a son in your arms." "No, my lord," she said, "man of God, do not deceive your servant."
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, "my lord, man of God" is a single form of address; splitting it across the speech attribution breaks the phrase and reads awkwardly aloud.

text: But the woman conceived, and at that time the next year she bore a son, just as Elisha had told her.
The child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the harvesters.
He said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
The servant lifted him up and brought him to his mother. He sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind her, and went out.
She called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so I can hurry to the man of God and come back."

versions.text: She called her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and a donkey, so I can hurry to the man of God and come back."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the parallel construction "one of the servants and one of the donkeys"; the parallel is lost with "a donkey." Also וַתִּקְרָא אֶל־אִישָׁהּ is "called to her husband" (he was in the field).

text: "Why go to him today?" he asked. "It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." "It is all right," she said.
She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on; don't slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite.
Run out to meet her and ask her, 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is the child all right?'" "Everything is all right," she said.

When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone; she is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and not told me."
Then she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Didn't I say, 'Do not raise my hopes'?"

Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the boy's face."
But the boy's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound, no response. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The boy has not awakened."
When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy, dead, lying on his bed.
He went in, shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
Then he got on the bed and lay on the boy, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he stretched himself out over him, the boy's body grew warm.
Elisha turned away and walked back and forth in the room, then got on the bed and stretched out over him once more. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite." He called her, and when she came, Elisha said, "Take your son."
She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. Then she took her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. While the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire and cook some stew for these sons of the prophets."

versions.text: Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. While the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire and cook some stew for the company of the prophets."
versions.explanation: The same Hebrew phrase (בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים) is rendered two different ways in one verse — "sons of the prophets" and "company of the prophets" — which may confuse a listener into thinking two groups are meant. Use one consistent rendering.

text: One of them went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine. He gathered some of its gourds and filled the fold of his cloak. When he came back, he cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.
They poured it out for the men to eat, but as they were eating the stew they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.

versions.text: They poured it out for the men to eat, but as soon as they tasted the stew they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כְּאָכְלָם is "as they were eating," not "tasted." The verb is אכל (eat), and the change also better sets up the following clause "they could not eat it."

text: Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people to eat." And there was no longer anything harmful in the pot.

versions.text: Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people to eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
versions.explanation: Minor clarity: the Hebrew implies the harm was removed after the flour was added; "no longer" makes the miracle clear for oral hearers.

text: A man came from Baal Shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain, along with some fresh heads of grain in his sack. "Give it to the people to eat," Elisha said.
But his attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" Elisha answered, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: 'They will eat, and there will be some left over.'"

versions.text: But his attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" Elisha answered, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: 'They will eat and have some left over.'"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew infinitives אָכֹל וְהוֹתֵר are impersonal; "there will be some left over" reads more naturally aloud and avoids the slightly clumsy "have some left over" repeated in v. 44.

text: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, just as the LORD had said.
